comments_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: from the mucosal lesion

technique: ZNF582m levels were determined using the “Epigene” ZNF582 DNA Detection Kit through quantitative methylation-specific PCR by using TaqMan-based technology with Light Cycler LC480
positivity_threshold: NR

site_selection_index_test: NR
technique: NR
positivity_threshold: NR

site_selection_index_test: scrape the entire lesion with the coverslip

technique: The lesion was scraped using a coverslip to collect cells, which were then spread onto a glass slide and fixed.
positivity_threshold: NR

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (IllumiScan® average fluorescence intensity)
index_test_reagent_name: IllumiScan® fluorescence visualisation device; average FI
site_selection_index_test: OMLs were selected after conventional oral examination under white light when they had features clinically suspicious for OPMD or early-stage SCC.
technique: Lesions were photographed under white light and then imaged with IllumiScan® in a dark room; irradiation brightness was maintained and the lens-to-lesion distance was approximately 30 mm.
positivity_threshold: Average FI cut-off of 98.5
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: average FI below cut-off of 98.5
blinding_index_test_examiner: No/unclear; ROI definition used intraoral photographs and intraoral findings by the attending physician.
comments_index_test: Average FI was one of three IllumiScan® ROC-derived metrics; the cut-off was defined by the Youden index rather than reported as pre-specified.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (IllumiScan® standard deviation of fluorescence intensity)
site_selection_index_test: OMLs were identified during conventional oral examination under white light; ROIs were then defined in the lesion area for IllumiScan® image analysis.
technique: IllumiScan® images were analyzed in ImageJ; the ROI fluorescence intensity was measured and the standard deviation was calculated.
positivity_threshold: SD cut-off of 11.2
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to intraoral photographs and intraoral findings for ROI definition.
comments_index_test: Same IllumiScan® image set was used for multiple ROC arms: average FI, SD, and CV; SD threshold appears ROC/Youden-derived.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (IllumiScan® coefficient of variation of fluorescence intensity)
site_selection_index_test: OMLs were identified during conventional oral examination under white light and suspected of OPMD or early-stage SCC before IllumiScan® imaging.
technique: IllumiScan® images were analyzed in ImageJ: ROI fluorescence intensity was measured, average FI and SD calculated, and CV calculated as (SD/average FI) × 10.
positivity_threshold: CV cut-off of 1.70
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to intraoral photographs/findings for ROI selection; blinding to other clinical information NR.
comments_index_test: The CV threshold was derived from ROC analysis using the Youden index rather than clearly pre-specified.

site_selection_index_test: Patients with suspected oral lesions were selected after detailed history and clinical examination.
technique: Participants rinsed with solution B for 20 seconds, the intended mucosal area was dried, solution A was applied, after 20 seconds participants rinsed again with solution B, and stain intensity was recorded.
positivity_threshold: local, stipules and concentrated blue stains
comments_index_test: No precancerous lesions were reported in the analyzed sample.

index_test_arm_label: Fluorescence visualization - subjective evaluation of FVL
site_selection_index_test: The control ROI was set at a distance away in the same sub-site of the oral cavity in normal mucosa in front of the lesion without FVL and oral mucosal lesions
technique: FV images were taken a room that was as dark as possible. The irradiating light was set perpendicular to the lesion and the irradiation range was set to about 10 cm
positivity_threshold: positive case as FVL and a negative case as only FVA or FVR
comments_index_test: Subjective FV arm; the paper also reports multiple objective image-analysis thresholds, so diagnostic arms may overlap in the same 502 patients.

index_test_arm_label: Fluorescence visualization - objective evaluation using MeanV
site_selection_index_test: The lesion ROI was selected as the area showing fluorescence visualization loss (FVL).
technique: FV images were obtained with the irradiating light perpendicular to the lesion and an irradiation range of about 10 cm.
positivity_threshold: MeanV cut-off 52.5 for detection of oral cancers.
comments_index_test: ORALOOK® and IllumiScan® were used randomly in this study.

index_test_arm_label: Fluorescence visualization - objective evaluation using MediV
site_selection_index_test: The lesion ROI was defined as the area of fluorescence visualization loss (FVL).
technique: The irradiating light was set perpendicular to the lesion and the irradiation range was set to about 10 cm.
positivity_threshold: MediV cut-off was set at 60.0 for detection of oral cancers.
comments_index_test: Objective MediV analysis was one of several image-processing metrics from FV images; ORALOOK® and IllumiScan® were used randomly.

index_test_arm_label: Fluorescence visualization - objective evaluation using CV
site_selection_index_test: The lesion ROI was defined as the area of fluorescence visualization loss (FVL).
technique: FV images were taken in a dark room as much as possible, with irradiating light perpendicular to the lesion and an irradiation range of about 10 cm.
positivity_threshold: CV cut-off 0.15
comments_index_test: ORALOOK® and IllumiScan® were both used, with instrument choice left to the attending physician.

index_test_arm_label: Fluorescence visualization - objective evaluation using skewness
site_selection_index_test: Regions of interest for the lesion and control area were established in FV images.
technique: FV images were analyzed by image processing using ImageJ software.
positivity_threshold: Skewness cut-off 0.71
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive threshold: skewness cut-off 0.71; direction NR
comments_index_test: Skewness was one of several objective image-processing metrics evaluated from the same FV images; arms are not independent.

index_test_arm_label: Fluorescence visualization - objective evaluation using VRatio
site_selection_index_test: The lesion ROI was defined as the area of fluorescence visualization loss (FVL).
technique: The irradiating light was set perpendicular to the lesion and the irradiation range was set to about 10 cm.
positivity_threshold: VRatio cut-off was set at 87.5% for detection of oral cancers.
comments_index_test: Objective VRatio arm from fluorescence visualization images; ORALOOK® and IllumiScan® optical instruments were used randomly.

index_test_arm_label: Fluorescence visualization - combined subjective evaluation, CV, and VRatio
site_selection_index_test: The lesion ROI was defined as the area of fluorescence visualization loss (FVL); the control ROI was selected in normal mucosa in the same oral sub-site away from the lesion.
technique: Fluorescence visualization images were obtained with the irradiating light perpendicular to the lesion and an irradiation range of about 10 cm.
positivity_threshold: Combination score cut-off 19.4 for detection of oral cancer.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: combined subjective evaluation + CV + VRatio score at/above cut-off 19.4
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to oral condition images for subjective evaluation.
comments_index_test: Combined arm was derived from multivariate-analysis significant factors and weighted using odds ratios; the study used ORALOOK® and IllumiScan® devices.

site_selection_index_test: oral cavity lesion or suspicious area
specimen_collection: The samples from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area were collected by a cytology brush.
technique: The conventional alcohol-fixed smears were stained according to the Papanicolaou method and interpreted by the cytopathologist.
positivity_threshold: “positive” indicated malignant cells present
comments_index_test: This row corresponds to the brush cytology and PAP staining arm; the study also evaluated brush cytology VPAC and oral gargle VPAC.

index_test_arm_label: Brush cytology and VPAC receptor positivity
site_selection_index_test: Oral cavity lesion or suspicious area
specimen_collection: Samples from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area were collected by a cytology brush.
technique: Harvested brush-cytology material on glass slides was fixed in 97% alcohol; TP4303 solution (0.5 µg) was added to cover the cells, followed by DAPI and fluorescent-microscope examination.
positivity_threshold: Presence of VPAC receptors indicated by dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus; reports were read as positive for VPAC receptors (malignant cells).
comments_index_test: NR

index_test_arm_label: Oral gargle and VPAC receptor positivity
site_selection_index_test: Whole oral cavity sampled by oral gargle with normal saline; no lesion-specific site selection for this arm was reported.
specimen_collection: Patients gargled with 20 cc normal saline for a few minutes and spat the contents into a collecting cup.
technique: The oral gargle fluid was centrifuged; sediment was placed on a glass slide, fixed in 97% alcohol, then processed using the VPAC receptor fluorescence procedure with TP4303 and DAPI.
positivity_threshold: Positive if cells showed TP4303 interaction as dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus, indicating VPAC receptor molecules around the cell surface.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark orange fluorescence around nucleus
comments_index_test: Figure caption appears inconsistent with the oral gargle arm because it describes cells prepared from voided urine.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: Each clinically identified oral lesion compatible with OPMDs or OSCC was examined and then scanned with GOCCLES®.
technique: The lesion/tissue was irradiated using an SDi Radii Xpert polymerizing lamp at 440–480 nm, 1500 mW/cm2, from 20 cm, and observed through the GOCCLES® device.
positivity_threshold: Lesions showing fluorescence loss, visible as brown or dark green areas through the device, were classified as GOCCLES® positive.
calibration_of_assessors: Same professional with specialized training in oral medicine performed the procedures; no formal calibration reported.
blinding_index_test_assessors: No; lack of examiner blinding was reported.
blinding_index_test_examiner: No; the same professional performed all procedures, so the GOCCLES® examiner was not blinded to other clinical information/procedures.
comments_index_test: Biopsy site selection was based on investigator judgment after the index-test procedures, raising potential incorporation/selection concerns.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: TB staining was applied to the clinically identified oral lesion(s) after visual examination, with lesion location and characteristics recorded.
specimen_collection: NA (in-vivo vital staining; no tissue or cellular specimen was collected for the index test).
technique: TB staining was performed following the technique described by Mashberg (1983).
positivity_threshold: Lesions with intense blue staining were classified as positive for TB; no staining or slight/diffuse staining was considered negative.
calibration_of_assessors: Same professional with specialized training in oral medicine performed the procedures; no separate calibration exercise was reported.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Lack of examiner blinding was reported; all procedures including biopsy site selection were performed by the same professional.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded; the paper reports lack of examiner blinding, though the exact scope regarding patient history or demographics is not specified.
comments_index_test: Potential risk of bias for the TB arm because the study reports lack of examiner blinding and all procedures were performed by the same professional.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
index_test_reagent_name: GOCCLES® device plus toluidine blue; concentration NR
site_selection_index_test: Patients with oral lesions compatible with OPMDs or OSCC were selected; lesions were clinically examined before GOCCLES® inspection and toluidine blue staining.
technique: After anamnesis and oral examination, lesions were inspected with GOCCLES® and stained with toluidine blue; combined results were evaluated when the two tests were concordant.
positivity_threshold: Combined positive when both GOCCLES® and toluidine blue were positive; combined negative when both were negative.
calibration_of_assessors: All procedures were performed by the same professional with specialized training in oral medicine.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not blinded / lack of examiner blinding reported.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded / lack of examiner blinding reported; the same professional performed all procedures including biopsy site selection.
comments_index_test: Combined diagnostic performance was calculated only for 18 concordant cases; discordant GOCCLES®/toluidine blue results were excluded from this arm’s analysis.

site_selection_index_test: Thorough intraoral clinical examination for the location of the most representative mucosal site for the white and red lesions.
technique: Patients rinsed with distilled water for one minute; 1% RB solution was applied for two minutes over the clinically assessed site; patients rinsed again with distilled water for one minute; staining intensity was visually evaluated as mild, moderate, intense, or negative.
positivity_threshold: Mild positive, moderate positive, or intense positive staining was considered positive; negative staining was considered negative.
comments_index_test: All three procedures were performed concomitantly on the same lesion, limiting time-lapse or positional differences between tests.

site_selection_index_test: at the same site
specimen_collection: Microbiopsy using a dermatological ring curette with a 3 mm diameter by scraping the lesional area gently with the sharp edge of the curette to obtain pinpoint mucosal bleeding and ensure basal-layer sampling.
technique: Scraped the intensely stained lesional area gently with the sharp edge of a 3 mm dermatological ring curette until pinpoint mucosal bleeding; tissue fragments were processed, embedded, sectioned, and H&E stained.
positivity_threshold: histopathological indicators of epithelial dysplasia (cellular and architectural changes)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: epithelial dysplasia on microbiopsy histopathology
blinding_index_test_assessors: Observer was blinded to the result of vital staining and scalpel biopsy.
comments_index_test: All three procedures were performed concomitantly on the same lesion; microbiopsy was one arm in a multi-index-test design alongside Rose Bengal staining.

index_test_arm_label: DNA aneuploidy by DNA image cytometry
site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush biopsy was performed at the same location of the lesion before scalpel biopsy.
specimen_collection: Brush sample collected by brushing the whole lesion with a liquid-based brush kit.
technique: DNA content status was analyzed using image cytometry according to the manufacturer's protocol.
positivity_threshold: at least 1 aneuploid cell with a DI ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: at least 1 aneuploid cell with DI ≥ 3.5
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA-ICM analysts were blinded to histopathological results.
comments_index_test: DNA aneuploidy arm; the study also assessed a modified risk model as a separate index-test arm.

index_test_arm_label: Risk model based on DNA aneuploidy with lateral/ventral tongue and non-homogenous features
index_test_reagent_name: DNA image cytometry combined with lateral/ventral tongue and non-homogenous lesion features
site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush biopsy was performed at the same lesion location before scalpel biopsy.
specimen_collection: Brush sample collected by brushing the whole lesion with a liquid-based brush kit.
technique: Risk model used the sum of scores for lateral/ventral tongue, non-homogenous type, and DNA aneuploidy from multivariate logistic regression.
positivity_threshold: Risk model score ≥ 4
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA-ICM analysts were blinded to histopathological results; blinding for clinical feature assessment was not reported.
comments_index_test: Combined model was developed in a 608-patient training set and validated in a 202-patient test set; threshold was optimized by Youden index.

index_test_commercial_name: GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System's (Changsha) DNA Image Cytometer
site_selection_index_test: Brush samples were obtained from the oral mucosal lesions; incisional biopsies were performed at the same locations where brush samples were obtained.
specimen_collection: The patient rinsed the mouth with water and the clinician gently scraped the oral mucosal lesions at least 10 times using a flexible cotton cytology brush.
technique: Brush samples were examined using liquid-based thin-layer cell preparation, Feulgen-thionin staining, and scanning with the GEMINI DNA Image Cytometer.
positivity_threshold: Abnormal DNA content if the aneuploid group had more than 3 nuclei, or the hyperdiploid group had 5% of total nuclei, or the tetraploid group had 10% of total nuclei.
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA image cytometry was performed blinded to the histological results.
comments_index_test: DNA quantitative analysis required specimens to contain at least 300 epithelial cell nuclei.

site_selection_index_test: manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites
technique: complete clinical interview followed by COE with manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites
positivity_threshold: classified the lesions into benign or malignant based on the clinical characteristics found
calibration_of_assessors: One general dentist had a 1-year training program in oral medicine; the other was unskilled.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Index test assessors performed COE in the absence of histological data.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to clinical information; COE was performed on the basis of clinical information.
comments_index_test: COE results are reported separately for unskilled and skilled general dentists, but this row represents the COE index-test arm overall.

site_selection_index_test: Vel-E was performed on lesions classified clinically as benign or malignant based on clinical characteristics and clinical information, before histological data were available.
technique: The VelScope device was held approximately 5 cm from the oral cavity to visualize natural tissue fluorescence; the operating theatre was darkened if needed.
positivity_threshold: In the presence of LAF, the Vel-E is defined positive
calibration_of_assessors: One of the two general dentists had a 1-year training program in oral medicine before performing Vel-E.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Index test assessors performed Vel-E in the absence of histological data.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to clinical information; Vel-E was performed on the basis of clinical information.
comments_index_test: Same VelScope arm interpreted separately by unskilled and skilled general dentists; diagnostic performance was reported separately for u-GD and s-GD.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions were included for cytopathological evaluation.
specimen_collection: Commercially available toothbrush (medium bristles) was used to obtain the material with minimal discomfort.
technique: For BR, patients rinsed the oral cavity with normal saline; material was obtained using a commercially available medium-bristle toothbrush and deposited onto a glass slide.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: BR was one of four cytology techniques evaluated; 27 cases had BR cytology, but histopathological comparison was available in 23 cases.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions were selected for cytopathological evaluation.
specimen_collection: Material was collected by modified scrape cytology using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon.
technique: Modified scrape cytology was performed using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: The SR technique was nondiagnostic in two cases overall.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions that were accessible for sampling.
specimen_collection: Material for the BRCC arm was collected using the modified brush cytology technique with a commercially available toothbrush with medium bristles.
technique: Brush-collected material was immersed in 15 mL normal saline, mixed well, and cytocentrifuged using program No. 1 at 1250 rpm for 3 minutes; this was named the BRCC technique.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: Multi-arm overlap: BRCC was evaluated alongside BR, SR, and SRCC in each case.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions accessible for sampling
specimen_collection: Scrape cytology material was collected using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon.
technique: Material obtained by scrape cytology was immersed in 15 mL normal saline, mixed well, and cytocentrifuged at 1250 rpm for 3 minutes; this was the SRCC technique.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: In the SRCC technique, the definitive diagnosis could not be offered in one case (3.7%).

index_test_reagent_name: Oral liquid-based brush cytology using Orcellex® brush
site_selection_index_test: Oral brush biopsy was performed before surgical biopsy; the exact lesion-site selection procedure for brushing was not further specified.
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy using Orelcex® brush under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsy.
technique: OLBC samples were preserved in ThinPrep® PreservCyt vials and processed into liquid-based cytology slides using the ThinPrep® 2000 processor according to manufacturer instructions.
positivity_threshold: NR; OLBC was graded into cytological categories rather than a clearly pre-specified binary positivity threshold.
comments_index_test: One OLBC slide was excluded because of a Papanicolaou staining defect; OLBC grading alone had reported accuracy of 95.07%.

index_test_reagent_name: DNA mismatch repair proteins immunocytochemistry: MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1 and PMS-2
site_selection_index_test: Oral brush samples using Orcellex® brushes were obtained from all participants directly before undergoing surgical biopsy.
specimen_collection: All patients underwent oral brush biopsy using Orelcex® brush under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsies.
technique: Standard immunocytochemistry staining was carried out on 4-μm cell-block sections for MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1 and PMS-2.
positivity_threshold: Cumulative index: 7.76-12 = No dysplasia; 5.51-7.75 = Low-risk lesion; 2.76-5.5 = High-risk lesion; 0-2.75 = OSCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: lower cumulative MMR index score; ≤7.75 indicates OED/abnormal lesion category and 0-2.75 indicates OSCC category
blinding_index_test_assessors: Slides were assessed blindly by two independent observers.
comments_index_test: Cumulative-index cut-off values were derived from ROC coordinates using Youden’s index rather than clearly pre-specified.

index_test_reagent_name: Combination of cumulative MMR index and OLBC grading scores
site_selection_index_test: Clinically diagnosed oral leukoplakia or oral squamous cell carcinoma lesions/participants were selected for testing.
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy using an Orelcex® brush under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsy.
technique: Combined index calculated as a combination of cumulative MMR index and OLBC grading scores.
positivity_threshold: Combined index: 8.26-12 = No dysplasia; 5.76-8.25 = Low-grade lesion; 3.76-5.75 = High-grade lesion; 0-3.75 = OSCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: combined index ≤8.25 for dysplasia/OSCC; OSCC category ≤3.75
blinding_index_test_assessors: ICC slides were assessed blindly by two independent observers; blinding to the reference standard is not explicitly specified.
comments_index_test: A substantial proportion of prepared cell blocks were excluded due to inadequate cellularity before the final 72-case analysis.

index_test_reagent_name: hBD-2 and hBD-3 antibody pairs from Peprotech
site_selection_index_test: Suspicious oral lesion and contralateral normal oral mucosa were sampled by cytobrush.
specimen_collection: Cytobrush collection from the suspicious lesion using pressure and 10 turns; the contralateral normal side was collected using the same procedure.
technique: Cell lysates from paired cytobrush samples were tested by sandwich ELISA for hBD-2 and hBD-3 using optimized Peprotech antibody pairs; BDI was calculated as the lesion hBD-3/hBD-2 ratio divided by the contralateral normal hBD-3/hBD-2 ratio.
positivity_threshold: BDI value at or above 1.25 indicates cancer and would necessitate biopsy.
calibration_of_assessors: A standard protocol was followed; formal assessor calibration or training was not otherwise reported.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Index test assessors were blinded to pathology-determined diagnoses until BDI scores were obtained.
comments_index_test: Although this row is anchored to Peprotech reagents, the external validation studies used Phoenix Pharmaceuticals ELISA kits rather than Peprotech.

index_test_reagent_name: fluorescent antibodies specific for hBD-3 or hBD-2
site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush samples were collected from OSCC lesional sites and contralateral sites of five OSCC patients and from five healthy subjects' left and right cheek (or tongue).
specimen_collection: For MICA, samples were collected in PBS and added to ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) containing vacutainer tubes.
technique: Cytobrush samples were injected into the MICA microchannel; retained cells were fixed, permeabilized, stained with DAPI and fluorescent antibodies to hBD-3 and hBD-2, imaged, and BDI was computed from hBD-3/hBD-2 fluorescence ratios.
n_patients_received: 10 (five OSCC patients and five healthy subjects)
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: MICA-BDI was a proof-of-principle point-of-care adaptation tested in a small OSCC-versus-healthy comparison, not the multicenter diagnostic validation against suspicious benign lesions.

index_test_arm_label: L1-SVM top four absolute multispectral autofluorescence features
site_selection_index_test: Images were acquired from the clinically suspicious oral lesion and a clinically healthy-appearing contralateral anatomical site.
technique: Multispectral autofluorescence endoscopy used 355 nm pulsed laser excitation and collected autofluorescence emission at 390 ± 20 nm, 452 ± 22.5 nm, and >500 nm bands; absolute spectral feature maps were used in an L1-SVM classifier retrained with the top four features.
positivity_threshold: Validation sample classified as cancer/precancer if its predicted image-level score was greater than or equal to the optimized threshold; benign otherwise.
comments_index_test: This arm used the best-performing L1-SVM model with the top four absolute multispectral autofluorescence features; it is a computer-assisted classifier rather than a simple visual autofluorescence interpretation.

index_test_reagent_name: Combined normalized autofluorescence intensities at 452 ± 22.5 nm and >500 nm simulating VELscope autofluorescence emission
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspicious oral lesions were imaged, along with a clinically healthy-appearing contralateral area.
technique: A linear L1-SVM model (C = 1) used a single spectral feature: combined normalized autofluorescence intensities at 452 ± 22.5 nm and >500 nm (I452,n + I500,n), simulating VELscope autofluorescence emission, trained and cross-validated using LOPOCV.
positivity_threshold: Validation sample classified as cancer/precancer if predicted image-level score was greater than or equal to the optimized threshold; benign otherwise.
comments_index_test: This arm simulated VELscope using a single autofluorescence feature from the multispectral imaging dataset; it was not an actual VELscope device examination.

site_selection_index_test: All patients immediately before undergoing surgical biopsies; specific oral site-selection procedure NR.
specimen_collection: OLBC using Orelcelx brush was performed on each patient under local anesthesia before surgical biopsy.
technique: Brush heads were preserved immediately in ThinPrep PreservCyt, transferred to the laboratory, processed into LBC slides using the ThinPrep 2000 processor, and Papanicolaou stained.
positivity_threshold: For the OED/OSCC analysis, OLBC positive was interpreted as low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, or OSCC; negative as undetermined significance or cyto OLP/OLL.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Yes—LBC slides were blindly and independently assessed by three assessors.
comments_index_test: 31 of 315 patients were excluded from analysis because of inadequate cellularity.

site_selection_index_test: Acetic acid solution was applied to the suspected oral lesions.
technique: AA solution was applied to suspected lesions on the first day; no further step-by-step technique was reported.
positivity_threshold: Acetowhite look after acetic acid application.
calibration_of_assessors: Identification, application, and post-staining assessment were standardized across examiners.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners were involved in screening/recruiting and stain application to prevent bias; explicit blinding to clinical information was not reported.
comments_index_test: All three stains were applied to the same participants/lesions; acetic acid and Lugol's iodine were applied on day 1. Reported analysis counts for acetic acid total 34 despite 45 subjects/lesions being described as assessed.

site_selection_index_test: LIS application to their suspected lesions
technique: On the first day, each patient received AA solution and LIS application to their suspected lesions.
positivity_threshold: NR
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not clearly reported; different examiners were used for screening/recruiting and stain application to prevent bias.
comments_index_test: Reported Lugol's iodine diagnostic 2x2 counts were TP 20, FN 3, FP 9, TN 2; these sum to 34 despite the study reporting 45 assessed cases.

site_selection_index_test: oral lesions
technique: The following day, the individuals were treated to TBS.
positivity_threshold: stained positive
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.
comments_index_test: All three vital stains were applied to oral lesions in the same study protocol and in respective order.

site_selection_index_test: Oral tissue/lesions were examined with Identafi® violet light to assess suspicious lesions for loss of autofluorescence.
technique: The Identafi® device was switched to violet light and used to examine lesions for loss of autofluorescence; lesions displaying LOA were blanched to assess diascopic fluorescence.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that displayed LOA were considered positive; lesions with no LOA or gain of autofluorescence were considered negative.
comments_index_test: Lesion-level analysis; positive reference standard was presence of dysplasia on histopathology.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Tissue reflectance (Identafi® green-amber light)
site_selection_index_test: Green-amber light was applied intraorally to the oral mucosa/lesions after prior Identafi® examination, to compare vasculature between normal and abnormal tissue.
technique: The Identafi® device was switched to green-amber light to visualize differences in vasculature between normal and abnormal tissue.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with diffuse vascularity that appeared darker were considered positive.
comments_index_test: Index-test arm shares the same 63 lesions as the Identafi® violet-light and toluidine-blue arms; diagnostic accuracy was reported lesion-level against dysplasia on histopathology.

site_selection_index_test: Lesions were stained with toluidine blue after screening with Identafi®.
technique: Patients rinsed with water for 20 s; 1% acetic acid was applied for 20 s; the area was dried; 1% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion with a cotton swab for 1 min; 1% acetic acid was then applied for 1 min; patients rinsed with water again.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue stain uptake was considered positive.
comments_index_test: Biopsy site selection incorporated toluidine blue positivity along with Identafi® findings and clinical judgment; diagnostic accuracy was reported at lesion level.

site_selection_index_test: The MB dye (1%) was then applied directly on the lesion with cotton bud for 30 seconds.
technique: The MB dye (1%) was then applied directly on the lesion with cotton bud for 30 seconds.
positivity_threshold: Dark royal blue/deep blue stains of MB were considered as positive retention.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark royal blue/deep blue MB stain
comments_index_test: Biopsy site selection was influenced by MB retention and LI staining, so reference sampling was not independent of the index-test procedures.

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (Methylene Blue and Lugol's Iodine Double Staining)
site_selection_index_test: Lesional and perilesional sites were stained; LI was applied to the lesional and perilesional sites after MB staining.
technique: Patients rinsed with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds, the target mucosa was dried, MB was applied directly on the lesion with a cotton bud for 30 seconds, excess dye was rinsed with 1% lactic acid, dye retention was assessed, and then 3% LI was applied to lesional and perilesional sites with a cotton bud for 10–20 seconds.
positivity_threshold: Double-staining result considered dysplastic/positive when LI was negative: pale yellow or unstained areas; LI dark brown was considered normal.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LI unstained or pale yellow
comments_index_test: Double-stain colour interpretation was noted as difficult, because mixed colour after LI application could be misleading.

site_selection_index_test: Suspicious oral cavity lesions were selected after clinical examination and stained with Toludine blue.
technique: After clinical examination, suspicious lesions were stained with Toludine blue.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue staining was considered positive for premalignant or malignant tissue; light staining or no colour was considered negative.
comments_index_test: Same 44 patients received both screening methods, so this arm overlaps with the NBI arm.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically selected lesions in the oral cavity with suspicion of malignancy.
technique: Patients underwent zero-degree endoscopic examination in white light, followed by NBI.
positivity_threshold: Altered or hypervascularity and increased capillaries (brown dots) were considered suggestive of malignancy.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: altered/hypervascularity with increased capillaries (brown dots)
comments_index_test: Same 44 patients received both screening methods, indicating multi-arm overlap.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, photographed the lesions, and selected the areas to be examined.
technique: The lesion was cleaned with a cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid, toluidine blue was applied with a different cotton tip for 30 seconds, excess toluidine blue was removed with 1% acetic acid, and the patient rinsed the mouth.
positivity_threshold: A positive lesion was defined as one whose color changed to blue; a negative lesion had no change.
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue results appear to include lesions from patients receiving toluidine blue application, with a separate combined toluidine blue plus vinegar group also reported in the study.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
technique: For acetic acid application, a gauze soaked with vinegar was applied to a clean and dry lesion for one minute.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was designated when a lesion changed to opaque white.
comments_index_test: The vinegar diagnostic table appears to include all lesions receiving acetic acid, including overlap with the combined-test group.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
technique: Application of vinegar was conducted first, followed by application of toluidine blue.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was indicated for a lesion with color changed to both opaque white and blue.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: opaque white and blue color change
comments_index_test: Combined-arm counts are inconsistent: narrative reports 27 lesions, but Table 4 reports 28 specimens from 24 patients and the table totals sum to 28.

site_selection_index_test: The main site of morphologically altered mucosa was selected and photographed.
technique: 1%TB is applied in 4 steps; first, rinsing of oral cavity with water for 20 s to remove debris, then application or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s, after that application or rinse with TB solution (1% W/W) for 20 s and finally application or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s to eliminate mechanically retained stains.
positivity_threshold: A royal blue or a navy blue stain as shown in Fig. 1 was considered as a positive result even if either the entire lesion or a portion of the lesion is stained or stippled.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: royal blue or navy blue stain
calibration_of_assessors: Dental surgeons in the selected institutions were trained by an Oral Medicine expert at their institutions.
comments_index_test: Histopathological diagnosis was available only for 60 patients despite 65 patients receiving TB testing.

site_selection_index_test: Autofluorescence examination using the Velscope was performed after conventional oral examination in participants with suspicious oral mucosal lesions.
technique: The VELscope autofluorescence examination was performed after conventional oral examination using the Velscope device.
positivity_threshold: Dark/brownish fluorescence observed through Velscope was considered positive for dysplastic changes within the mucosa.
calibration_of_assessors: VELscope examination was performed by a dental surgeon/trained field investigator; no formal calibration procedure was reported.
blinding_index_test_examiner: VELscope was performed after conventional oral examination and provisional clinical diagnosis, so blinding to clinical examination was not reported.
comments_index_test: Some lesions with autofluorescence patterns other than complete FVL were grouped with FVR for statistical analysis because no specific criteria existed.

index_test_arm_label: Other (White Light Examination / Conventional Oral Examination)
site_selection_index_test: All selected subjects with suspicious oral mucosal lesions underwent conventional oral examination at CHCs/PHCs before VELscope examination.
technique: Conventional oral examination was performed under white operatory light, and a provisional clinical diagnosis was recorded.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: positive on white light examination
calibration_of_assessors: Conventional oral examination was performed by trained field investigators.
comments_index_test: White light examination had 12 no-result cases; these were not included in the 2×2 diagnostic table, which totaled 238.

site_selection_index_test: the usual routine clinical examination according to the standard protocol
technique: only white light examination was performed
positivity_threshold: CA was positive when a suspect lesion was seen
comments_index_test: Biopsy was discretionary after a suspect lesion in either CA or VELscope assessment, so not all patients received the reference standard.

site_selection_index_test: In all patients, the oral cavity was examined using VELscope; suspect regions were marked according to the Roed-Petersen protocol.
technique: The oral cavity was examined with VELscope in a separate room with dimmed lights; patients and examiner wore safety goggles, and suspect regions were marked according to the Roed-Petersen protocol.
positivity_threshold: A suspect finding in the VELscope assessment was defined as loss of fluorescence.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded/unclear: the same experienced maxillofacial surgeon examined all patients; no explicit blinding to clinical information was reported.
comments_index_test: VELscope was used as an adjunct after routine clinical examination; biopsy was performed only when a suspect lesion was identified clinically or by VELscope and the surgeon judged biopsy necessary.

index_test_arm_label: Oral colposcopy using Reid's Colposcopic Index (RCI)
index_test_reagent_name: 5% acetic acid solution and Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to the lesion; no further oral site-selection procedure for the index test was reported.
technique: After wiping the mucosa with saline, vascular patterns were viewed using the green filter at high magnification (≥×30); 5% acetic acid was applied for about 60 seconds to assess aceto-whitening at low magnification (≤×20); then Lugol's solution was applied to assess iodine uptake at low magnification (≤×20).
positivity_threshold: The cutoff value to segregate dysplastic lesions from nondysplastic lesions was 5 according to the RCI.
comments_index_test: Same colposcopic examination was evaluated with both RCI and the Swede scoring system; this row uses the RCI arm.

index_test_arm_label: Oral colposcopy using the Swede scoring system
index_test_reagent_name: 5% acetic acid solution and Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water)
site_selection_index_test: clinically suspected OPMDS
technique: After wiping the mucosa with saline, vascular patterns were viewed with the green filter at high magnification; 5% acetic acid was applied for about 60 seconds; then Lugol's solution was applied to assess iodine intake.
positivity_threshold: 8 according to the Swede scoring system
comments_index_test: Same colposcopic examination was evaluated using both RCI and Swede scoring system; index-test arms are overlapping rather than independent.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clearly visible oral lesions showing apparent variation from normal healthy mucosa.
specimen_collection: Cell samples were collected using the Orcellex® Brush.
technique: After twisting the brush ten times, the brush head was transferred directly into alcohol-based liquid in the BD SurePath™ Collection Vial and transported to the laboratory.
positivity_threshold: Cytology was considered positive when classified as doubtful or positive; negative cytology was considered negative.
calibration_of_assessors: No explicit calibration reported; cytology assessors were board-certified oral pathology experts practicing for more than 7 years.
comments_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: Clearly visible oral lesions showing apparent variation from normal healthy mucosa were selected for brush biopsy.
specimen_collection: At least five brush smears per lesion were collected with the nylon brush.
technique: The brush head was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times.
positivity_threshold: Cytology results classified as doubtful, suspicious, or positive were considered tumor-cell positive; only negative was considered tumor-cell negative.
comments_index_test: Nylon-brush arm used five brush smears per lesion, whereas the rigid-brush arm used one obtainment; this difference may affect diagnostic accuracy.

site_selection_index_test: clearly visible oral lesions which showed apparent variation of the normal healthy mucosa
specimen_collection: only one obtainment using the rigid brush was performed routinely
technique: The head of the brush was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times; the head was then washed out in the preservation vial.
positivity_threshold: the results 'doubtful', 'suspicious' and 'positive' were summarized as 'tumour cell positive'; only 'negative' was reported as 'tumour cell negative'
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: cytology positive, suspicious, or doubtful; negative: cytology negative
comments_index_test: Rigid-brush arm was a later, separate cohort used from June 2012 to February 2018.

site_selection_index_test: All patients were subjected to VELscope examination
technique: performed approximately from a distance of 3–4 inches and noted the nature of tissue fluorescence in terms of fluorescence retention or loss
positivity_threshold: loss of fluorescence (FVL) and appear dark
comments_index_test: Index tests were applied sequentially; VELscope was followed by vital tissue staining.

site_selection_index_test: Methylene blue vital staining was applied on the suspicious oral area.
technique: After VELscope documentation, vital staining including methylene blue was performed on the suspicious area; stain uptake was assessed and photographs were documented.
positivity_threshold: Deep blue stains, local, stippled and patchy were considered positive; faint blue stains that were wide, shallow and easily washable were considered negative.
comments_index_test: All patients underwent multiple index tests; vital tissue staining was performed after VELscope examination.

site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue staining was applied on the suspicious area after VELscope examination.
technique: Staining procedures using toluidine blue were performed on the suspicious area; uptake of stain was considered positive and no or light uptake negative. No detailed step-by-step toluidine blue protocol was reported.
positivity_threshold: A dark blue (royal or navy) stain of either the entire lesion or a portion of it was considered positive.
comments_index_test: All patients appear to have received multiple index tests, including vital staining; toluidine blue concentration was not reported.

site_selection_index_test: Applied on the suspicious area.
technique: Staining procedures using vital stains, including Lugol's iodine, were performed on the suspicious area.
positivity_threshold: uptake of stain was considered as positive for dysplasia, no uptake of stain or light uptake of staining was considered as negative for dysplasia
comments_index_test: Overlapping multi-arm design: all patients received VELscope followed by vital tissue staining procedures.

site_selection_index_test: After localizing the lesion
specimen_collection: A 23–24G needle attached to 10 ml disposable plastic syringe was used.
technique: After localizing the lesion, fine-needle aspiration was performed using a 23–24G needle attached to a 10 ml disposable plastic syringe.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: FNAC and scrape cytology were both performed, but diagnostic-accuracy results are reported for cytology/scrape and aspiration together rather than separately for FNAC.

site_selection_index_test: pathological sites, frequently from mucosal lesions and from other representative sites
specimen_collection: Scrape smears were collected using a wooden Ayer's spatula from pathological sites, frequently mucosal lesions and other representative sites.
technique: Scrape smears were done by wooden Ayer's spatula from pathological sites, frequently from mucosal lesions and from other representative sites.
positivity_threshold: NR
comments_index_test: The study included both FNAC and scrape cytology; methods describe scrape collection, but cytology results are reported generally as cytological diagnosis rather than clearly separating FNAC from scrape cytology.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence: direct fluorescence visualization (direct FV)
index_test_reagent_name: Direct fluorescence visualization device using blue excitation light (400 to 460 nm)
site_selection_index_test: After turning off the room light, the oral cavity was viewed with direct FV.
technique: The handheld unit projected excitation light onto the oral mucosa and provided a viewing port coaxial with illumination for fluorescence visualization.
positivity_threshold: Tissue that showed a distinct reduction in the normal pale green and appeared as dark green to black was classified as FV loss (FVL).
comments_index_test: Biopsy decisions were based on standard clinical features and not on direct FV examination.

site_selection_index_test: Lesional and perilesional tissue was assessed for visual fluorescence retention (VFR) and visual fluorescence loss (VFL).
technique: Direct visual examination was performed using the VELscopeVX handpiece, assessing lesional and perilesional tissue for VFR and VFL.
positivity_threshold: VFL+
comments_index_test: Biopsy site selection attempted to cover both COE and VEL positive regions.

index_test_reagent_name: VELscope (C Ultra by Technomax Corporation, Pune, Maharashtra)
site_selection_index_test: clinically suspicious oral lesions
technique: After COE, autofluorescence visualization (AFV) was achieved by a handheld VELscope (C Ultra by Technomax Corporation, Pune, Maharashtra).
positivity_threshold: AFL: Loss of fluorescence.
comments_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspicious lesion areas in the oral cavity after clinical examination and photography.
technique: Lesion areas were pre-treated twice with 1% acetic acid using a cotton bud for 20 seconds and rinsed with water; 1% toluidine blue was then applied with a cotton bud for 10–20 seconds; the lesion was decolorized with 2% acetic acid for 20–30 seconds and photographed.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue was considered positive for lesions suspicious of malignancy; light blue retention was considered positive for premalignant lesions unless proved otherwise by biopsy; no retention was considered negative.
comments_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: Performed on fixatives from biopsy specimens received from cases with provisional diagnosis of oral pre-malignant lesions and oral malignant lesions; specific oral cavity site-selection procedure was not reported.
specimen_collection: Specimen consisted of 10% formalin-fixed punch, incisional, or excisional biopsy specimens measuring more than 1×1 cm; cytology used the leftover formalin from the original specimen bottle.
technique: Biopsy specimens were shifted to fresh fixative; original bottle fixative was centrifuged at 3000 rpm for five minutes; supernatant was discarded; sediments were washed twice in normal saline; smears were prepared on albumen-coated slides, fixed in 95% ethanol with 3% glacial acetic acid, and stained with Papanicolaou stain.
positivity_threshold: Negative: Class I; positive for OPMDs: Class II and III; positive for oral malignant lesions: Class IV and V.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: cytologic atypia/dysplasia or malignancy classes
comments_index_test: Sediment cytology was performed on leftover biopsy fixative rather than as an in-vivo pre-biopsy oral cavity test; the article notes it cannot provide definite diagnosis.

site_selection_index_test: One oral lesion smear was taken from each patient before biopsy using a cytobrush all over the lesion
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear was taken from each patient before biopsy using a cytobrush all over the lesion and stored at PreservCyt Thinprep (Hologic).
technique: Slides were stained according to Papanicolaou and classified using an adaptation of Remmerbach et al.
positivity_threshold: Positive/high-risk cytology was defined as high-grade lesions suspicious for malignancy and squamous cell carcinoma; low-risk included negative and low-grade lesion samples.
comments_index_test: Brush cytology was reported as a standalone arm and also contributed to the combined Brush cytology + DNA-ICM arm; some samples were inadequate due to scant cellularity or overlap.

site_selection_index_test: all over the lesion
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear was taken from each patient before biopsy using a cytobrush all over the lesion and stored at PreservCyt Thinprep (Hologic).
technique: slides were uncovered in xylene and stained by the Feulgen-Schiff method (Merck)
positivity_threshold: The sample was considered aneuploid if a stemline DNA index was <0.90 and >1.10 or <1.80 and >2.20 or <3.60 and >4.40 or if there were cells with exceeding 9c content.
calibration_of_assessors: Nuclear content analysis was performed according to the 4th European Society for Analytical Cellular Pathology (ESACP) Consensus in DNA image cytometry.
comments_index_test: Samples were considered inadequate at cytologic and/or DNA ploidy analyses due to scant cellularity or high overlapping rate in 16 cases.

site_selection_index_test: The test was applied to the clinically selected oral cavity lesion; the smear was taken all over the lesion before biopsy.
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear was collected from each patient before biopsy using a cytobrush over the whole lesion and stored in PreservCyt Thinprep.
technique: Three cytologic slides were prepared per lesion sample using Cellspin I; slides were Papanicolaou-stained and classified for cytology. For DNA-ICM, the same slides were uncovered in xylene, Feulgen-Schiff stained, calibrated with normal oral epithelial nuclei, and at least 200 nuclei were measured using MotiCyte software to classify euploid versus aneuploid.
positivity_threshold: Positive when both methods were positive: brush cytology positive/high-risk and DNA-ICM positive/aneuploid.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: both brush cytology and DNA-ICM positive
comments_index_test: The combined analysis appears to include only cases classified as both negative or both positive, giving an analyzed denominator of 54; inadequate cytology and/or DNA ploidy samples were also reported.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically visible lesions in the oral cavity were assessed by clinical examination.
technique: All patients were examined by the consultant Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon and grouped as benign, premalignant, or malignant.
positivity_threshold: Premalignant or malignant lesions were considered positive; benign lesions were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: clinical diagnosis premalignant or malignant
comments_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: applied to the lesion
technique: 1% Acetic acid mouth wash for 20 seconds after rinsing with water, then 1% Toluidine blue applied to the lesion with a cotton swab, followed by Acetic acid mouth wash to remove extra stain
positivity_threshold: positive or negative irrespective of the intensity of the stain
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue staining was compared with clinical assessment and histopathology; the paper reports low specificity and high false positives.

site_selection_index_test: biopsies were taken from the area with most clinical suspicion (by inspection and palpation) of the pre-malignant or malignant lesion
technique: On local examination by inspection and palpation, the location, size of the lesion, extent of local infiltration, oral hygiene, and cervical lymph node status were assessed.
positivity_threshold: Clinical Suspicion of premalignant or Malignant Lesion
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: clinical suspicion of premalignant or malignant lesion
calibration_of_assessors: The clinical examination was done by a single expert otorhinolaryngologist.
comments_index_test: Alternate sampling was used; no proper randomization method was adopted.

site_selection_index_test: Applied over the oral lesion, covering approximately a 2 cm margin all around the lesion.
technique: Mouth rinsed with water; 1% acetic acid rinse for 20 seconds; lesion dried with gauze; 1% Toluidine Blue applied gently with a cotton swab for 1 minute over the lesion and approximately 2 cm margin; 1% acetic acid rinse for 1 minute; dye uptake observed under proper light and exposure.
positivity_threshold: Positive if the lesion diffusely or partly stained dark blue (royal or navy blue), or had a stippled appearance.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue or stippled stain
comments_index_test: Biopsy in the Toluidine Blue arm was guided to the area with maximum stain uptake; allocation was by alternate sampling rather than proper randomization.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to patients with symptoms and signs suggestive of oral premalignant lesions or suspected oral malignancy after comprehensive head and neck examination.
technique: Mouth rinsed with water for 20 s to remove debris; 1% acetic acid applied for 20 s to remove ropey saliva; 1% toluidine blue oral rinse for 20 s; 1% acetic acid rinse repeated to remove mechanically retained stain; final rinse with water.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that exhibited dark blue staining were deemed positive for premalignant or malignant tissue, while those with light staining or no color were considered negative.
comments_index_test: Concentration inconsistency: the text/protocol reports 1% toluidine blue, but figure captions report 0.1% solution.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to the clinically suspected oral PMD lesion(s) after rinsing and drying.
technique: Five percent acetic acid was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds.
positivity_threshold: Positive if the lesion appears opaque white (acetowhite).
calibration_of_assessors: The principal investigator was trained in the specialty of oral medicine; no specific acetic-acid calibration was reported.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to clinical information before staining; the principal investigator obtained patient history and clinically examined suspected lesions.
comments_index_test: Same lesions received acetic acid followed by toluidine blue and biopsy; tests were applied sequentially rather than independently.

site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied to the clinically suspected oral lesion.
technique: 1% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds and decolorized with acetic acid.
positivity_threshold: The lesion was considered toluidine blue positive if it retained blue color after the staining.
calibration_of_assessors: The principal investigator was trained in the specialty of oral medicine; no specific toluidine-blue calibration procedure was reported.
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied after 5% acetic acid in the same lesions, indicating sequential multi-arm testing.

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (2% Toluidine Blue-containing electrospun fiber patch)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to lesions from patients with suspected OPMDs, ulcerations suggestive of malignancy, or nonhealing ulcers persisting for >2 weeks without identifiable cause.
technique: History taking and oral examination; apply 1% acetic acid with cotton tip for 20 s; apply electrospun patch containing 2% toluidine blue; apply 1% acetic acid with cotton tip for 20 s; then biopsy.
positivity_threshold: Positive defined as dark blue staining; pale or no staining was negative.
comments_index_test: The study did not compare the electrospun toluidine blue patch with standard toluidine blue staining protocols.

site_selection_index_test: all study participants with suspicious OPMDs underwent another oral examination by the same clinician using OralID®
technique: OralID emits visible blue light (435–460 nm) directly into the oral cavity, allowing the clinician to view tissue fluorescence during the oral exam.
positivity_threshold: lack of fluorescence or dark, or a combination of bright green/white green fluorescent and dark areas
calibration_of_assessors: The dentist was highly trained in detecting OPMDs with the conventional oral examination
comments_index_test: The same dentist performed the conventional and fluorescent oral evaluations, which the authors noted could result in report bias.

site_selection_index_test: Oral examination using the Velscope before incisional biopsy; no more specific site-selection procedure was reported.
technique: A blue light (400–460 nm) was directed onto the oral tissues, and the emitted fluorescence was assessed visually.
positivity_threshold: Lesions exhibiting loss of autofluorescence (FVL) appeared as dark areas, suggesting dysplasia.
calibration_of_assessors: Initially, 10 patients were examined to calibrate the visualization of colours for consistent assessment across the study.
comments_index_test: The narrative reports that Velscope identified 51 participants as positive, which appears inconsistent with the 40-patient sample.

site_selection_index_test: oral mucosal lesions identified during participant screening were subjected to DrOroscope examination
technique: On blue light exposure, normal tissues reflect green fluorescence, while abnormal tissues show loss of fluorescence and appear dark.
positivity_threshold: a loss of fluorescence indicates dysplasia
calibration_of_assessors: The examiner was trained in the operation of DrOroscope and interpreting its results.
comments_index_test: After image analysis, DrOroscope categorized lesions into variable, borderline, and severe.
